newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf, Talisman get Indonesia boost.
newsitem.headline: Gulf, Talisman get Indonesia boost.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd and Talisman Energy Inc said on Tuesday that Indonesian state oil company Pertamina extended their Corridor Block production sharing contract to 2023.
The extension moves 140 million gross barrels of oil equivalent reserves to the proved from the probable category, the companies said.

"Gulf is booking 500 billion cubic feet (400 BCF net of royalties) of gas and three million barrels (two million barrels net) of natural gas liquids, or approximately 85 million BOEs," Gulf senior vice-president Dick Auchinleck said in a statement.

"Although the reserves associated with the Corridor Block Gas Project were technically certified as proved in 1995, we retained them in the probable category until major milestones such as the contract extension were achieved."
Talisman said its Indonesian subsidiary would book about 330 BCF (270 BCF net) of proved gas reserves and two million (1.6 million net) barrels of liquids, translating into about 55 million BOE.
The Calgary-based firms said an important aspect of the contract extension was a new 65-35 government/contractor split for gas.
The split means the government wouldl receive 65 percent of profits after cost recovery, down from 70 percent under previous contract terms.

Gulf and Talisman said the improved terms would provide a higher incentive for gas exploration and development in the Corridor Block and support an Indonesian government goal of ensuring the project become the cornerstone for development of a trans-Sumatra gas pipeline.
Corridor is designed to produce 300 million cubic feet of gas per day. Start-up is scheduled for mid-1998, with full shipments starting in the fourth quarter of this year.

Gulf unit Asamera (Overseas) Ltd has a 54 percent interest in the Corridor Block, Talisman's Talisman (Corridor) Ltd has a 36 percent interest and Pertamina has 10 percent. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
